reasoning_content:
This is using Go 1.22+ ServeMux's wildcard pattern `{repositoryURL}`. In Go's ServeMux, `{repositoryURL}` is a wildcard that matches up to the next slash, but... actually, in Go 1.22's ServeMux, `{repositoryURL}` is a wildcard that only matches a single path segment. Hmm, but then, a URL that contains slashes (like `https://gitlab.opencode.de/...`) shouldn't match. Wait — in Go 1.22+, the pattern segment `{name}` matches only a single path segment (no slashes). There's also a special wildcard `{name...}` that matches the remainder of the path. So `GET /api/v1/repositories/{repositoryURL}/sarif` — since `{repositoryURL}` matches only a single segment, a URL like `/api/v1/repositories/https://gitlab.opencode.de/open-code/badgebackend/badge-api/sarif` should match `{repositoryURL}` = `https:`... no wait, that's wrong. `https://gitlab...` contains slashes, so it can't be a single segment.

Actually, wait. When I made the request `GET /api/v1/repositories/https://gitlab.opencode.de/open-code/badgebackend/badge-api/badges/security`, a 307 Temporary Redirect to `/api/v1/repositories/https:/gitlab.opencode.de/...` came back — the double slashes got collapsed into single ones. This is typical Go net/http behavior... actually, the Go 1.22+ ServeMux does not collapse slashes. It's more likely that the handler itself is doing a redirect. Let me look at the handler code and check how the repository URL is being parsed.
